raw:
Morning brings the low blue light of storm clouds and the scent of fresh bread downstairs.

You wash, dress in the charcoal coat, and make it to breakfast with time to spare. Ashara and Rashid are already at the table, arguing quietly over a point from last night’s drills.

“Your guard opened on the third exchange,” Ashara says.

“It adjusted.”

“It opened.”

Rashid looks across the table at you. “Morning, Rowan. The eggs are safe. Avoid the pale sauce unless you enjoy regretting things before noon.”

Thessaly has a small stack of cards beside her plate, arranged in rigid suits and ranks. “Dena explained the rules again. They remain inefficient.”

“They’re cards,” Caelindra says from behind a book.

“Then they could be better cards.”

At the ninth bell, the residents make their way across the quadrangle to the Conclave seminar room. Lightning moves slowly beneath the far bridges, far enough below that the storm seems almost decorative.

Inside, fifteen chairs surround the oval table, though only seven are occupied. The framed Accords on the walls carry the Covenant in scripts you cannot read. Aldric chooses a place facing the door; Ysolde takes a seat near an open window where the cold air reaches her. Ashara and Rashid sit apart, still conducting their argument in occasional glances.

Professor Elara Windwhisper enters precisely on the bell. Her silver hair is braided close to her head, and she carries no notes.

“Welcome to the Conclave,” she says. “For four years, you will study the structure you may someday be asked to preserve, amend, or survive.”

She looks around the table, including you without lingering on the Garvey signet.

“Today is orientation. We will cover Academy procedure, residence expectations, access privileges, and the first term’s work. Tomorrow, you begin Covenant Law.”

She takes the remaining chair at the head of the oval table and opens a thin folder.

Outside, another branch of lightning blooms beneath the Nexus.
